coverageSpotVerification.detail: See trace.md section 3. No manifest in the registered clique-coverage-manifest.v1 format exists at all; the lane ships coverage/m{1..6,8}.json auto-emitted by scripts/acceptance.mjs from whatever assertionId string each suite test supplies. M1 keys exactly the frozen suite-required set and every mapped test exercises its observable. M2 keys all 22 frozen suite-required ids honestly except m2-a22/a23, whose mapped tests verify API pagination and never touch the 'scrolling loads the next page' clause that the client in fact fails; that is read as weak coverage in good faith, so M2 is NOT adjudicated and the failure is carried instead as two failed assertions and defect d-05. M3, M4, M5, M6 and M8 re-use the frozen id namespace for lane-local, differently-numbered assertions, so the mapped test does not exercise the claimed observable and the collision conceals wholly unimplemented checklist items: m4-a01 (photo message end-to-end) maps to react-toggle-counts; m4-a03 (video message) to react-deleted-refused; m4-a09 ('edited' label) to unsend-nonauthor-refused; m5-a09 (people search) to search-window-reaches-history; m5-a01 - a [grader]-class id a suite manifest may not claim at all - to accent-roundtrip-sync; m8-a03 (7-day bucket) to same-principal-live-delivery; m8-a05 (Trending) to dual-offline-converge; and none of M6's frozen suite-required ids (m6-a08..a11, a13) appear at all while m6-a01..a07, the simulator assertions, are occupied by API-level offline tests, presenting native coverage that does not exist. No fabricated results were found: every mapped test exists, runs, and reports truthfully about what it actually tests.

defects.summary: The Following feed silently drops all but 40 followed accounts: snapback/feeds.q merges `[f.followed] for f in follows[viewer] first 40 by byFollower`, so a user following more than 40 accounts never sees the rest, with no error and no indication.
defects.evidence: trace.md#52-two-structural-findings-at-the-envelope — at the named O5 fixture u0500 (500 follows) walking every page of the Following feed surfaces 41 distinct authors (u0500 plus 40 followed). Reproduced on the dev instance with a purpose-built 45-follow user: 45 targets, followingCount 45, 5 authors missing, and the missing indices were 6, 16, 17, 27, 39 - an arbitrary 40 of the 45 edges, not the newest 40. grading/probes/followcap.mjs, grading/probes/o5-repeat.mjs

defects.summary: View-once media is gated only in the UI: the asset layer is never revoked, so the bytes are fetchable before openViewOnce is ever called and remain fetchable by both recipient and sender after the view is consumed.
defects.evidence: trace.md#6-defects-beyond-the-checklist d-02; grading/probes/m5-a06b.mjs — pre-open authenticated fetch SERVED 2104 bytes; after VIEW_ONCE_CONSUMED, messages.messageById still exposes message.photo and a freshly minted URL on a fresh recipient session serves 2104 bytes, as does the sender's. A non-member is correctly refused E_ASSET_NOT_READY, so this is not a cross-user leak.

defects.summary: Any signed-in user with a profile can rewrite the app-wide edit/delete windows and every disappearing TTL, defeating the server-side window enforcement for all users.
defects.evidence: trace.md#6-defects-beyond-the-checklist d-03; snapback/schema.q:329-330 and 342-343 guard cliqueConfig and disappearingTtls with `insert/update <- exists profiles[viewer]`. Demonstrated in grading/windowconfig-demo.log: an edit past the 60 s window was refused EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED; a second, unrelated user then called setWindowConfig(999999, 999999); the same edit committed and the recipient read the rewritten body. The fixture values were restored immediately and re-verified.

O1.anchorsCited: At the ~30 anchor: 'core features partially work; several checklist items fail'. Below the ~60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') once the adjudication applies, because five of the eight in-scope milestones score their checklists not-passed.
O1.justification: Independent execution passes 81 of 119 in-scope assertions (M1 13/13, M2 25/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 9/12, M6 1/13, M7 0/9, M8 6/18) = 68%. The 119 denominator is counted from the assertion arrays themselves; the manifest's `counts` block predates the m2-a25/a26/a27 additions and understates M2. Applying the coverage-manifest adjudication (M3, M4, M5, M6, M8 score their checklists not-passed per the frozen rule) leaves 38 of 119 = 32%. Both numbers are published here so the placement is auditable: it is dominated by the adjudication and by M7 never being attempted, not by product breadth. M1-M4 are genuinely strong on independent execution; M5 loses people search, grouped global search and view-once asset revocation; M6 has no push seam, no custom-client demo, no API.md and no native/simulator artifact; M7 was never attempted (no suite, no poll ops, no schema, no iOS bundle); M8 has no 7-day breakdown, no Trending and no digest. Platform-proof artifacts are present and real for every attempted milestone (verified Hermes bytecode v96), but the M6/M8 native offline proofs the 90-anchor names are absent entirely. Evidence: trace.md sections 2, 3, 4.

O2.anchorsCited: At or just below the ~30 anchor: 'multiple high-severity defects in core flows'. Far from the ~60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path').
O2.justification: One blocker and six majors beyond the checklist, most in core flows: the Following feed silently drops all but 40 followed accounts (d-01, demonstrated at the named O5 fixture and reproduced independently); conversation history is unreachable past 30 messages (d-04); the feed's Load more button is a no-op (d-05); Insights totals are wrong past 60 posts (d-06); view-once media is never revoked at the asset layer (d-02); any signed-in user can rewrite the global edit/delete windows and disappearing TTLs (d-03); Search drains whole chat corpora to the client (d-07). Placed at 25 rather than 30 because seven high-severity defects is more than 'multiple' and five of them are wrong-data or broken-flow defects on the happy path. Offsetting evidence that kept it from going lower: the cross-user trust boundary is solid - 18 of 20 authorization probes correctly denied, including every attempt to read, write, restyle or moderate another user's chat, and delete-side asset revocation works correctly. Evidence: trace.md sections 5.2 and 6.

O5.bandRationale: First-match order 0 -> 30. Band 0 does not fire: I re-ran the full scale replay independently on a fresh instance (167,244 actions in 1,063 s) and the invariant manifest conformed at the 10%, 50% and final checkpoints with figures identical to the lane's receipt, including 'o5 ok' on the named fixtures; I separately confirmed u0500 followingCount=500, u0900 followerCount=900 and u0500's 100 memberships through the app's own reads; and the replay completed rather than exhausting a cap. Band 30 fires on 'any degradation rule fails'. Two of the frozen M8 rules fail: (a) Insights - the brief states that a page-and-count-client-side implementation 'fails structurally, not just on latency', and app/insights.tsx is exactly that, chaining three client-side profilePosts pages and summing them (also demonstrated wrong at 65 posts, defect d-06); (b) Trending - there is no Trending implementation at any checkpoint to measure against the 3x rule, the tab renders the literal placeholder 'Trending lands in M8.'. No probe timed out, errored or OOMed. The remaining published rules pass on measurement (deep paging p95 ratio 0.86; celebrity read 1.10; celebrity write 1.00; cold-start sync of 100 conversations in 60 ms; global search p95 27 ms), and the 500-follow fanout rule passes only on best-of-3 (ratios 3.80 / 1.13 / 8.77 / 3.36 at host loads 22-38, best 1.13) and does so partly because the read is structurally truncated to 40 of 500 follows (defect d-01). Evidence: trace.md section 5.

notes: PROBE SET: no holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped entirely, wave.probeSetSha256 records the literal 'none-uncommitted', and probeResults is empty. No probes were invented. The O5 envelope measurements reported in the O5 rationale and in trace.md section 5.1 exercise the brief's PUBLISHED degradation contract on the grader's own reproduced scale corpus; they are deliberately not reported as probeResults and they bear on O5 only, never on O3. CALIBRATION: this grader family has not passed the calibration gate, so calibrationPassed is false and the record labels this grade 'uncalibrated-grader'; sameFamilyGraded is false (this is not an abort-fallback regrade). RUN RECORD: lane.runRecordPath points at a file that does not exist - the lane wrote no run-record.json - so this report is graded entirely from receipts, source, and independent execution. M8 RESULTS: this schema's assertionResults key pattern is ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$ with additionalProperties:false, which predates the 2026-08-11 M8 amendment, so the 18 M8 assertions cannot be keyed there. They were executed and are recorded in full in trace.md section 4.8: 6 pass (m8-a01 six lifetime totals; m8-a02 likes-received refresh; m8-a13 same-account cross-device live; m8-a14 cross-device read state; m8-a15 dual-offline convergence; m8-a16 receipts after flush) and 12 fail (m8-a03, m8-a04 - no 7-day breakdown; m8-a05, m8-a06, m8-a07 - Trending renders the placeholder 'Trending lands in M8.'; m8-a08 through m8-a12 - no digest implementation anywhere in the lane; m8-a17, m8-a18 - no native artifact). Those 6 passes are the M8 contribution to O1's 81/119. O3/O4 NULL: O3 is null because its only permitted input is the wave's secret rotated probe set, which does not exist for this run, and because the M6 coverage adjudication removes the m6-green predicate; O4 is null because the m6-green predicate fails under the same adjudication - and independently, the only permitted O4 input, mechanically checkable simulator choreography artifacts, does not exist for this lane at all, so no observation of native offline behaviour was available to score. NO WEIGHTED TOTAL: three O-dimensions are null and M7 was never attempted, so this lane is not a complete lane and no weighted total, efficiency statistic or cross-lane comparison is computed here - those are the harness's and publisher's jobs.
